items.quote: rest = max(0.0, 100 - sum(c for c in given if c > 0))
items.what: loot_chances clamps an overfull loot group: when a group's explicit chances sum past 100, the leftover is clamped to 0 and the group's equal-share (chance 0) rows get a 0% chance, with no report
items.why: The project convention is that generators raise or report instead of clamping bad data. On the pinned classic-db dump the clamp fires for 12 groups (11 in creature_loot_template, e.g. entry 14507 group 1 sums to 200 with 6 zero-chance rows; 1 in gameobject_loot_template, entry 16591 group 1 sums to 108 with 7). Their zero-chance items silently vanish from ns.RecipeSources drops (scroll_drops needs share > 0) and from ns.GatheredBy (gathered needs 10%), and another 57 overfull groups pass through with shares totalling over 100%. Nothing is printed or counted, so the generated drop chances look authoritative. Count and print the overfull groups (as keep() does for omitted NPCs) or raise.
items.reason: Recounted on tools/.cache/classicdb-22b5146.sql.gz: 69 grouped loot groups sum past 100 (65 creature, 3 gameobject, 1 reference), 12 of them hold zero-chance rows that loot_chances floors to 0, and main() prints nothing about any of them. An in-memory run of generate() with those groups removed changes Data/Sources.lua (709 to 699 recipes; recipe 16660's drops from NPCs 6109, 10184, 12397), so shipped drop chances rest on unreported out-of-contract data, against the Conventions line 'generators raise instead of clamping bad data'; no Do-not-flag or Settled entry covers it and tools/README.md does not document the clamp.

items.quote: resale = auction * 0.95 if mode == "auction" and auction else None
items.what: model_craft_value restates Model.CraftValue (Model.lua:294) with the auction cut inlined as 0.95 instead of Model.lua's AUCTION_CUT = 0.05 (Model.lua:287), and with Python truthiness in place of Lua's.
items.why: A change to AUCTION_CUT would not reach the screenshots. Truthiness drift: Lua `auction and auction * (1 - AUCTION_CUT) or nil` treats auction == 0 as truthy, giving resale 0 and returning (0, "auction") when there is no vendor price; the Python treats 0 as falsy and returns (None, None). Also `mode == "none"` returns (None, None) vs Lua's single nil (harmless). Not reachable with the current scene (mode is hard-coded "vendor" at :204 and AUCTION has no zero price), so latent. The other named ports match exactly: round_money == Model.RoundMoney (same unit thresholds, floor(+0.5), max 1); model_recipe_cost == Model.RecipeCost (`is None` equals Lua `not` for numeric/nil values, empty list returns 0 in both); model_chance/model_color/model_cost_per_skill_up match with the 0-based index shift.
